messages:
maria: Quick sync — I'm drafting a short PRD for quota + billing flows. Need decisions on: metering point (ingress vs generated tokens), default quota policies, grace behavior, and overage semantics. Customer asks: Finlytics wants soft-limits; HealthSys needs per-project caps.
lin: token-based metering + per-route attribution seems simplest implementation-wise. request-count is noisy for chat.
ryan: agree token-based, but we need a clear mapping for embeddings vs chat tokens (embedding = input tokens only). I'll draft conversion examples.
sasha: design note — UI must surface: burn by route, model, and SKU; timeline + projected spend. mock here: http://figma.redwood/quotas/mock1 (preview).
helen: heads-up from sales: a few enterprise deals require per-user sub-quotas inside an account. Important for renewals.
maria: proposal for scope: MVP = account-level quotas (tokens/window) + per-route overrides (no nested user billing). Mark per-user sub-quotas as "enterprise+" feature. Comments?
lin: ok for MVP. Edge cases: cached completions should not re-bill tokens. Also streaming partial failures — how do we meter aborted streams?
ryan: for cache: only bill when response generated from model (set header X-Redwood-Cache: HIT/ MISS). For aborted streams, bill tokens consumed by the model; client-side partial reads shouldn't change meter.
sasha: ACs (short):
- UI shows current consumption and % of quota by day/week/month.
- Admin can set grace credits and overage policy.
- Alerts for 80/90/100% with webhook/slack.
- Billing report matches meter for last 3 months.
maria: sample rate-limit rule syntax for engineering (informal):
```
rate_limit:
  scope: account
  metric: tokens
  limit: 1000000
  window: 30d
  grace: 50000
  overage_action: allow_overage  # options: reject, queue, allow_overage
  attribution: per_route    # options: per_route, per_model
```
lin: implementation notes: prefer soft enforcement for hosted (allow_overage + invoice) and hard reject for free-tier. We'll need efficient counters sharded by account + window.
ryan: billing semantics decision needed: immediate charge for overage vs invoice at period end. My preference: invoice at period end with pro-rate reporting; immediate charge only for credit-card customers who opt-in.
helen: sales + customers prefer predictable behavior: they'd rather have a small grace buffer + email alerts than surprise charges.
maria: acceptance criteria (final):
1) Metering: tokens counted consistently for generation/embedding, with cache exclusion header.
2) Quotas: account-level limits enforceable, per-route overrides honored.
3) Overages: default = soft (allow + invoice), configurable to hard reject for free-tier or customer opt-in.
4) UI: admin page + alerts + CSV export for last 3 months.
5) API: endpoints to query remaining quota, set overrides, and webhook for thresholds.
lin: edge cases to call out in PRD:
- time-window alignment after daylight saving changes; use UTC windows.
- account transfer between orgs: migrate usage counters safely.
- sudden burst: autoscaling vs queueing decisions — limit how many queued requests per account.
ryan: telemetry: add meter tag breakdown: model, route, prompt_type, cached. Need that in billing exports.
sasha: small UX ask: show projected month-end usage based on rolling 7-day average. Also allow admins to add manual credits (grace).
maria: next steps:
- lin to write infra/impl RFC with counters and rate limit API (due EOD Fri).
- ryan to write billing semantics doc (invoice vs immediate) with sample invoices.
- sasha to update mocks for admin UI + alert flows.
- I'll consolidate PRD (ACs + scope) and post for review.
helen: I'll surface the proposal to Finlytics + HealthSys, get feedback on per-user sub-quotas.
deploy-bot: spec doc updated: /docs/prd/quota-flows-1775239876.md (preview deployed) :white_check_mark:
